newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures called lower as APIs disappoint.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures called lower as APIs disappoint.

text.p: IPE oil futures were expected to start business lower on Wednesday after U.S. industry stock figures disappointed by showing a smaller than expected drawdown in crude and gasoline, brokers said.
IPE gas oil futures were anticipated opening $1 to $1.50 lower after closing yesterday up $2.50 at $167.75 a tonne.

IPE Brent crude will start 10-15 cents down on yesterday's settle of $18.81, brokers said. The front month jumped 30 cents on Tuesday in the belief American Petroleum Institute figures would show a bullish drop in primary storage numbers.
"We are in for a temporary setback," said one broker.
While the API data showed U.S. crude stocks held in primary storage fell 4.36 million barrels in the week ended June 27 to 317.96 million barrels, most of the drop was on the west coast.

Gasoline stocks fell 1.23 million barrels to 204.23 million, but the critical figures for the east coast actually showed an increase. "The APIs are not as bullish as we first thought," said one broker. "Gasoline stocks are still above this time last year."
But the shock will be eased by still strong supportive factors, such as tight physical markets and absent Iraqi barrels.
"The idea is to consolidate above the range we broke out of, which means staying above $18.50 on the Brent and above $19.50-60 on the WTI," said one broker.
Some dissenting voices suggested the effect of the APIs would be minimal, with dealers preferring to wait for the Department of Energy report to confirm them.
But weaker SIMEX quotes, at $18.65/$18.70 for August, suggested the market was preparing for a fall.
"The feeling is that the market is a bit overpriced and if it does come off people may jump on it," said one broker.
